grh_5da6a166ed6dcbe73f82.title: The Female of the Species
paragraphs: Entomologist Prudence Hastings arrives with a forged letter from the governor and persuades the Texas Rangers to send Ranger Chet Gearing with her to the headwaters of Salado Creek, supposedly to collect grasshoppers. Her real purpose is to recover one hundred thousand dollars in stolen gold for her husband, escaped killer Cody Bancroft. Bancroft and fellow fugitive Davey Gross murder a ranch couple on their way to the cache, then reunite with Prudence, capture Chet and leave him tied over an ant hill to die. Chet survives long enough to join the pursuing Rangers, and a gunfight and chase destroy the gang: Gross is killed, Prudence dies after Bancroft throws her from their overloaded horse, and Bancroft is captured with the recovered gold.

[[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Anne Burr, Sam Edwards, Vic Perrin, Tyler McVey, and [[person|parley-baer|Parley Baer]]. Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Ted Sherdeman as writer, and Lorne Greene as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_5d76d0b01b317b14b5a1.title: Words at War 44-01-18 (32) War Tide
paragraphs: A dramatization of Lin Tai Yi's War Tide follows young Loyin as war destroys the ordinary life of her Chinese family. Her brother goes to fly against the Japanese, her father dies after setting fire to his shop, and Loyin helps lead her mother, grandmother, sister-in-law and little brother through invasion, violence and flight; her grandmother even uses her nine-fingered hand to frighten away a threatening soldier by claiming leprosy. Reunited with the wounded Shen, Loyin accepts his proposal and the story closes on the idea of the war tide as the anger, courage and endurance that keeps people moving forward despite continuing danger.

Leader as director, Edith Sommer as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.

grh_5dc53b32a063686f260a.title: The White Brigade
paragraphs: Belgian civilian Jean Boucher joins the White Brigade resistance after the German occupation and takes part in espionage, sabotage and escape work while his family lives under constant threat. The Gestapo closes in, Jean is eventually killed while trying to escape, and his wife Denise loses their child after the Germans take her away. When the occupiers threaten to execute one hundred hostages unless the killer of a German officer confesses, Denise falsely claims responsibility so the hostages will be freed. Facing death herself, she tells a priest that sacrifice has become part of the resistance oath she and Jean accepted.

The cast includes Ned Wever, Les Damon, Berry Kroeger, Abby Lewis, and Joseph Boland. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Ruth Brooks as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.447e90e58c28e7c3|The White Brigade]]. Robert Goffen is credited as author and Ruth Brooks adapted it for radio.

grh_5d96257eae14833e8282.title: Apron Faced Sorrel
paragraphs: Sixteen-year-old Clay Fenton arrives for a summer on a ranch determined to hide his terror of horses, a fear dating from the accident that killed his father and scarred Clay when he was a small child. After being mocked and thrown by a difficult apron-faced sorrel, Clay secretly whips the horse nearly to death and runs away when the animal's reaction exposes what he did. Britt catches him and learns that Clay's cruelty grew out of fear. When Britt's horse Scar later saves Clay from a rattlesnake, Clay's attitude begins to change, and caring for the injured sorrel eventually turns fear and hatred into trust.

The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Britt Ponset]].

grh_5d17c4c22efc8c85a49d.title: The Third Woman
paragraphs: During the war, Corporal Harry Lime is dressed as a civilian colonel and sent by Allied intelligence to learn why agent Brunell is withholding the true location of a German underground rocket factory. In Istanbul, Harry discovers that the Germans are holding Brunell's younger sister Julie inside their embassy and using her to force false reports. Harry promises to free Julie in exchange for the real factory information. He enters an embassy reception, overpowers an armed guard, finds Julie and escapes with her through a window into firemen's rescue nets arranged in advance. Brunell provides the intelligence, although Harry later learns another agent had already supplied enough information for an air raid on the factory.

This [[show|the-lives-of-harry-lime|The Lives of Harry Lime]] broadcast aired on December 7, 1951. It is listed as episode 19 in the archive. The cast includes [[person|orson-welles|Orson Welles]] and Anton Karas. Other credited names include Tig Roe as director and Harry Alan Towers as producer.
The surviving recording runs about 27 minutes. Characters credited in this version include [[character|Harry Lime]].
